podcast.body: Olivia Newton-John won a Grammy for Female Pop Performance in 1974 for this song. This win occurred in a year that also saw other significant musical achievements, including Stevie Wonder's Grammy for "Fulfillingness's First Finale." "Olivia Newton-John won a Grammy for Female Pop Performance for I honestly love you."

This song earned Olivia Newton-John a Grammy for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance the year after "Let Me Be There" won for country. "Olivia won won a Grammy for I Honestly Love You the following year for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance."

This song was the number one track on the charts the week ending October 5th, 1974, which was the same week Stevie Wonder's "You Haven't Done Nothin'" reached number five. Its chart success illustrates the prevailing taste for less politically heavy pop music at the time. "The number one song that week was I honestly love you by Olivia Newton John"

This was the second of Olivia Newton-John's five consecutive top ten pop hits that also crossed over to country radio. Written by Jeff Barry and Peter Allen (who initially wanted to keep it for himself), the song won her a Grammy in 1975 for Female Pop Vocal performance and a Grammy for Record of the Year (shared with John Farrar). Its nomination at the Country Music Awards caused controversy among purists. It was Olivia's first number one pop song, reached number six on the Billboard Hot Country chart, and re-entered the digital song sales chart at number 39 in 2022 after her death. "I honestly love you."

Written by Peter Allen and Jeff Barry, this ballad of unrequited longing, described as "lyrically country but classically pop," was almost recorded by Allen but became a phenomenon for Olivia Newton-John. It reached number six on Hot Country Singles and went all the way to the top of the Hot 100, becoming her first American number one hit and spending two weeks at that position. "I honestly love you. Reach number six on Hot Country singles and went all the way to the top of the Hot 100."
